key_insight: EdgeDAM demonstrates that distractor-aware memory for single-object tracking can be redesigned without costly segmentation/mask prediction, enabling robust, continuous tracking at real-time speeds on resource-constrained mobile devices.
problem_solved: Bridges the gap between high-accuracy distractor-aware trackers (which rely on segmentation and attention-driven memory updates) and the need for low-latency, low-compute single-object tracking on edge/mobile hardware.
method: Replace segmentation- and mask-dependent distractor handling with a lightweight, feature-level distractor-aware memory mechanism tailored to bounding-box SOT.
Use compact feature representations and efficient memory update rules to suppress distractors while avoiding mask prediction and heavy attention layers.
Optimize the model for mobile deployment through computationally efficient backbones and runtime-friendly design choices (e.g., reduced FLOPs, quantization-friendly operations).
impact: Enables practitioners to deploy robust single-object trackers on smartphones and embedded devices without the latency and energy costs of segmentation-based approaches, widening real-world applications (AR, robotics, surveillance).
visual_elements: Architecture diagram contrasting segmentation-based distractor pipelines vs. EdgeDAM's lightweight memory flow

paper_title: EdgeDAM: Real-time Object Tracking for Mobile Devices
paper_authors: Syed Muhammad Raza, Syed Murtaza Hussain Abidi, Khawar Islam, Muhammad Ibrahim, Ajmal Saeed Mian
